Subject: POC / Trial planning: Workload intake & success criteria - Acme Health

Tom — thanks again for the call today. Great context on the EHR summarization use case and the SSO requirement. Per our discussion, attaching a short POC plan and a workload intake sheet so we can size the trial and propose the Dedicated/Hosted configuration that makes sense.

Top-line summary / asks: 
- Success criteria: 90%+ accuracy on extractive summaries vs your QA set; p50 end-to-end latency <200ms for single-turn prompts during steady-state; no more than 2% error/timeout under 95th percentile traffic during the trial.
- Evaluation plan: we'll run a 2-week trial with a fixed test corpus (~5k representative records) + live shadow traffic for 48 hours. We'll instrument token counts, latencies, and failure rates and share dashboards.
- Workload questions we need from you (see attached spreadsheet): typical RPS, expected concurrency, distribution of prompt/completion token lengths, burst expectations, and any regulated data flags.
- Proposed timeline: intake + config this week, infra prep + dry run next week, trial start on Jun 22 for 2 weeks.

Next steps (owner): 
1) Tom / Acme: complete workload-intake-template.xlsx with realistic RPS and token distributions by EOD Thu (owner: Tom)
2) Redwood: prep POC plan and pre-warm testing infra (owner: Ben & Dylan)
3) CS: define success checkpoints and reporting cadence (owner: Marissa)

Attachments: [Attachment: POC-plan.pdf (application/pdf) - 160KB] [Attachment: workload-intake-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) - 25KB]

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC / Trial planning: Workload intake & success criteria - Acme Health

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers inline: 

> typical RPS
We see about 8 RPS steady-state for the summarization endpoint across our web UI, peak bursts up to ~220 RPS during daily report runs (5–10 minutes), and occasional larger bursts (~400 RPS) during scripted backfills (rare, scheduled at night).

> expected concurrency
Our UI typically has about 12 concurrent users hitting the summarization endpoint during business hours; however the batch report process spawns ~60 concurrent worker threads during peak backfill windows.

> token lengths
Average prompt length: ~95 tokens (mostly patient context + instructions). Average completion: 180 tokens. Max combined token length observed in our dataset: ~1800 tokens (long discharge notes).

> regulated flags
PHI is present; we will need Private deployment or a strict Hosted contract with SOC2 + HIPAA BAAs. We'll follow up with legal on the BAA.

I'm attaching an exported traffic sample (see Drive link) and I'll fill out the intake spreadsheet by EOD Thu as requested.

—Tom
Tom Hayes | Platform Lead, Acme Health

Tom — this is perfect, thank you. A few notes and clarifying items before we kick off infra work: 

1) Bursts: our initial recommendation is to provision for steady-state 10 RPS + autoscale headroom to handle 250 RPS bursts with a short warm-up strategy. For the rare 400 RPS backfills we recommend scheduling during an isolated window and using batch inference if possible. Dylan — can you validate whether continuous batching + KV cache will help mitigate cost during the 5–10 minute burst windows?

2) Token ceilings: good to note the 1800-token max — we'll test for seq length degradation and ensure the model quantization/profile we pick handles 2k-ish contexts.

3) PHI / Compliance: we can move this POC under Redwood Private (VPC) or a Hosted instance with a BAA — I've flagged legal. Marissa — please outline the compliance checklist and timing for proof-of-concept in a reply.

Proposed updated timeline: intake completed Thu Jun 11 (you), infra validation mid next week (Jun 15–18), POC start Jun 22. If intake slips we'll target a POC start Jun 29.

I'll start drafting infra tasks and share a pre-warm test plan.

Best,
Ben
